title: When does Subgroup Balance Matter? Predicting Performance Sensitivity from Latent Separability
abstract: arXiv:2512.09496v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Unequal representation of demographic groups in training data poses challenges to model generalisation across populations. Standard practice assumes that balancing subgroup representation always optimises performance. However, recent empirical results contradict this assumption: in some cases, imbalanced data distributions actually improve subgroup performance, and in others, subgroup performance is unaffected by the absence of an entire subgroup during training. We propose the latent separation hypothesis, which states that a fine-tuned model's dependence on subgroup representation is determined by the degree of separation between subgroups in the latent space of the pre-trained model. We formalise this hypothesis, provide theoretical analysis, validate it empirically across four vision and language datasets, and present preliminary evidence of a causal role through regularisation experiments. translated_title: 子群平衡何时重要？基于潜在可分离性预测性能敏感性
translated_abstract: 训练数据中人口子群的不均衡表示给模型在不同人群上的泛化带来了挑战。通常的做法假设平衡子群表示总是能优化性能。然而，近期的实证结果与这一假设相矛盾：在某些情况下，不均衡的数据分布实际上会提升子群性能；而在另一些情况下，即使训练中完全缺失某个子群，子群性能也不受影响。我们提出了潜在分离假设，即微调后的模型对子群表示的依赖程度由预训练模型潜在空间中各子群之间的分离程度所决定。我们对这一假设进行了形式化表述，提供了理论分析，在四个视觉与语言数据集上进行了实证验证，并通过正则化实验提供了其因果作用的初步证据。最后，我们展示了如何量化……
tldr: 该论文提出“潜在分离假设”，指出微调模型对训练数据子群平衡的依赖程度由预训练模型潜在空间中子群间的分离程度决定，并通过理论分析与四个视觉及语言数据集上的实证和正则化实验验证了这一假设。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the latent separation hypothesis—that a fine-tuned model's dependence on subgroup balance is determined by the degree of separation between subgroups in the pre-trained model's latent space—validated through theoretical analysis, experiments on four vision and language datasets, and preliminary causal evidence from regularisation experiments.
